$comment: Data order is a function of (data_seed + epoch, len(dataset)) ONLY -- it does not depend on
the model. Verified on this branch: NumpyDataLoaderBase._build_global_indices does
get_rng(self.seed + self.epoch).shuffle(arange(len(dataset))) (data_loader.py ~line 674),
and get_rng is np.random.Generator(PCG64(seed)) (data/utils.py:585-586).
So the SAME --data-seed gives every arm a byte-identical token stream IF AND ONLY IF all of
the following also match. Any one of them differing silently breaks the pairing while every
run still trains and reports a plausible number.

must_match_across_every_cell_being_paire.sequence_length: identical (enters total_size via instances_per_batch = global_batch_size // sequence_length)
must_match_across_every_cell_being_paire.dataset_release: identical -- len(dataset) is in the shuffle domain AND in the indices-cache filename
must_match_across_every_cell_being_paire.steps: identical (a shorter arm consumes a prefix, not the same stream)
must_match_across_every_cell_being_paire.chunk_size_and_shuffle: left at config defaults; do not override per arm

pairing_preconditions.consequence: A cell that changes ANY of these is not paired with the others on data order and must be analysed as an independent sample.

$comment: Init seeds CANNOT be paired ACROSS arms. Arms have different tensor inventories (KDA-HH R=2
widens w_k/w_v/w_b and the k/v convs by R; GDN2 has w_w that KDA does not; the gated-conv
arm adds gate tensors), so a single RNG stream diverges at the first differing tensor and
every draw after it is unrelated. Reusing one integer across arms buys NO variance reduction
and must not be claimed to.
It is recorded, and REUSED IDENTICALLY FOR THE SAME ARM IN RUN 2, because that is what makes
run 2's repeated base-KDA arm a true replicate of run 1's rather than a fresh sample.

plumbing_verified_on_this_branch..edullm/train_core6_arm.py: PLUMBED. build_config passes init_seed=opts.init_seed into build_arm -> TransformerConfig.llama_like -> cls(...) -> TransformerConfig.init_seed, which reaches the Transformer constructor and the generator that actually draws weights (see the comment block at train_core6_arm.py:623-640). --init-seed default 12536.
plumbing_verified_on_this_branch..edullm/train_on_corpus.py: NOT PLUMBED. It exposes --data-seed only; there is no --init-seed. Its config carries init_seed=12536 (line 341) and calls seed_all(config.init_seed) (line 803), but weights come from TransformerConfig.init_seed, whose default is 0 (nn/transformer/config.py:326). Every 'n seeds' on that entrypoint is n data orderings of ONE initialisation.
plumbing_verified_on_this_branch.run_1_entrypoint: .edullm/train_core6_arm.py -- REQUIRED. train_on_corpus.py cannot vary the init component at all.

init_seed_semantics.guard: train_core6_arm.py:1582 refuses the run when config.init_seed != config.model.init_seed. Both are set together from --init-seed, so they can only diverge via a dotlist override (`init_seed=99` or `model.init_seed=42`) that moves one. NEVER override either field; pass --init-seed.
init_seed_semantics.weight_draw_default_never_used: None of the integers below is 0 or 12536, so a cell that silently fell back to a default is visible in the summary JSON rather than indistinguishable from a real cell.

not_small_sequential_integers: 0 and 12536 are the two defaults on this entrypoint; using them makes 'the flag did not reach the draw' indistinguishable from 'the flag reached the draw'.

Data order is keyed on (seed + epoch). With seeds 0,1,2 a cell at epoch 1 draws the same order as a cell at seed 1 epoch 0 -- an alias that a multi-epoch or resumed run can hit silently. Spacing the data seeds 10,007 apart makes aliasing impossible at any epoch count this study can reach.
Distinct decimal digits make a transposed seed in a submitted command visible by eye against the table.
seed_choice_rationale.construction: data_seed(r) = 200000 + 10007*r ; init_seed(arm_i, r) = 100000 + 3001*i + 10007*r  (i = arm_index below). 10007 and 3001 are primes, so no two cells collide -- verified: 24 integers, 0 duplicates. RECORDED AS LITERALS BELOW; the formula is documentation, not the source of truth.

locked_run_parameters.$comment: Locked 2026-08-08. These are pairing preconditions, not just cost inputs -- see pairing_preconditions above. A cell that differs on any of them is not paired.
locked_run_parameters.attempts_note: PINNED. The olmo-core-train profile defaults to 2, which doubles cost and flips the approval gate.
locked_run_parameters.throughput_basis_note: Conservative 20-step figure. A 200-step run read 455,789; that higher number is a run-length artifact and is NOT the planning basis.
locked_run_parameters.makespan_note: 6-way concurrency. Batch array jobs refill slots as they free, so makespan is sum-of-cells/concurrency, not serial waves. The 3 kda-hh-r2 cells run ~2x slower (non-chunked sequential Triton kernel) and are the long pole.

run_2.note: kda-paper is re-run on the IDENTICAL (data_seed, init_seed) pairs from run 1. Its purpose is twofold: it is run 2's internal baseline for the within-run K3 contrast, AND run1(kda-paper,r) minus run2(kda-paper,r) is a free per-replicate drift check on image, kernel and platform changes.

endpoint_keys.$comment: Exact keys in the JSON that .edullm/train_core6_arm.py summarise() prints on rank 0 (train_core6_arm.py:1471-1543). This is the only channel the platform reads results back through.
endpoint_keys.secondary_trajectory: sliced_eval (null when --slice-mask-uri is empty); plus the W&B 'train/CE loss' series
endpoint_keys.must_not_be_used_as_an_endpoint: last_loss (final TRAIN loss). A decay-to-zero LR schedule ends at a mechanically lower train loss at equal held-out quality, and can invert the comparison. first_loss is kept only as an init sanity check (expect ~ln(vocab) = 11.52 at vocab 100,352).
